name: generate_plugin_scaffold
description: Generate (or regenerate) a complete local plugin on disk: profile.json, plugin.py (the udi_interface Controller, with wiring methods always tool-generated and override-method bodies supplied here), any extra node-class files, main.py, version.py, server_entry.json (the exact local-install registration payload), requirements.txt (always includes udi_interface, plus any extra_requirements), install.sh (the executable script server_entry.json's 'install' field names by filename -- not a literal command), README.md, LICENSE.md (third-party attribution for every licensed source referenced, plus a plain MIT grant for this plugin's own code), tests, an append-only context.md iteration note, and sources.md (a deduped record of every evidence source gathered for this plugin, accumulated across sessions). Refuses if no developer has been commissioned yet for this workspace (call configure_developer first), if no evidence has been gathered this session (call search_store_plugins/search_github_plugins/search_web/fetch_reference first), if the profile fails validate_profile's checks, if override_bodies names an unknown method, or if anything generated appears to contain a real secret value -- OAuth client_id/client_secret are always written as a fixed placeholder, filled in for real after install via configure_plugin(key='oauth'). If any target file already exists, the first call returns the conflict list and writes nothing; call again with confirm_overwrite: true once the customer has agreed to overwrite. Follow with install_generated_plugin to actually register/install/start it.

location.description: The subdirectory name under the server's plugin output root to write this plugin into. Reuse the 'location' from list_generated_plugins/read_generated_plugin when updating an existing plugin.

profile.description: The Dynamic Profiles wire document -- top-level 'editors'/'nodedefs'/'linkdefs' lists, the same shape polyglot.getJsonProfile()/read_generated_plugin use. Internally wrapped and checked with the same structural validation validate_profile runs before anything is written.

controller_class.description: The Controller class name to generate in plugin.py. Defaults to 'Controller'.

controller_module.description: The module (filename without .py) main.py imports the controller class from. Defaults to 'plugin'.

version.description: The plugin version string written to version.py and passed to polyglot.start(). Defaults to '1.0.0'; bump on every regeneration that changes behavior.

node_classes.description: Extra device Node subclasses beyond the Controller, as {filename_without_py: full_python_source}, for profiles with more than one NodeDef.

override_bodies.description: Full Python method source (the 'def ...():' line through its body, properly indented as a class method) for each override this plugin needs, keyed by method name: start, stop, discover, shortPoll, longPoll, processConfig, parameterHandler, customParamHandler -- plus handle_custom_request and one '_<tool_name>' helper per server_entry.aiTools entry when server_entry.ai_enabled is true. Any name not supplied gets a safe no-op stub. Any other key is rejected. These fire in a fixed real-world order -- START, then CONFIG (processConfig), then CUSTOMPARAMS (parameterHandler), then CONFIGDONE -- and the tool-generated wiring already blocks start() until CONFIGDONE (or a timeout); write each override for its own place in that order rather than assuming config/params are already available earlier than CONFIGDONE. See the system prompt's 'Write override bodies for the real startup order' section for the full contract.

server_entry.description: The developer/tool-defined registration spec -- becomes server_entry.json, the exact PUT /api/plugins/store/local/entry body install_generated_plugin sends.

runAs.description: OS account the plugin process runs as. Defaults to the commissioned developer's configure_developer(default_run_as=...) value, or 'admin' if that wasn't set either.

customParams.description: A flat {field_name: value} object -- one entry per customer-facing config field (API keys, hosts, intervals). 'value' is each field's seeded initial value, commonly an empty string ('') or a minimal placeholder-like hint -- NOT documentation and not a real value (the customer fills in the real value afterward via configure_plugin). This is PG3's 'customparams' shape exactly -- not the richer typed-list shape ('customtypedparams') with per-field type/isRequired/defaultValue, which this tool does not generate. For the actual user-facing explanation of these fields, use the separate top-level custom_param_docs input, not this map.

authorize.description: True if this plugin needs OAuth against the target API.

oauth.description: OAuth endpoint config when authorize is true: auth_endpoint, token_endpoint, scope, addRedirect, addScope, token_parameters. Never include a real client_id/client_secret -- omit them and the placeholder is filled in automatically.

ai_enabled.description: True only if this plugin exposes AI-callable tools via CUSTOMREQUEST.

aiPrompt.description: Static developer-authored prompt text describing this plugin's AI tools.

aiTools.description: Each declared AI tool: {name, description, params?}. Every entry needs a matching '_<name>' helper in override_bodies.

nsdata.description: A one-time, developer-authored seed value handed to the plugin before it has ever run. Rarely needed -- not something a customer edits (that's customParams), not a secret (that's oauth). Omit unless a spec specifically calls for pre-seeding a value the plugin can't derive or ask for itself.

isyAccess.description: True if this plugin needs any communication with eisy/ISY itself -- nodes, programs, commands, properties, etc. Defaults to false.

requireEisyui.description: True only if this plugin is meaningless outside eisyUI (no standalone configuration path at all). The developer must know this about their own plugin. Defaults to false.

extra_requirements.description: Extra pip requirements (e.g. 'requests>=2.31.0') this plugin's generated code needs beyond udi_interface, written to requirements.txt. install.sh (an executable script running 'pip3 install -r requirements.txt', named by server_entry.json's 'install' field) is always generated automatically.

devd.description: Only for plugins needing direct serial/USB hardware access. {vendor_id, product_id, name} (vendor_id/product_id as 4-hex-digit strings, e.g. from detect_usb_device) renders the devd.conf hardware-attach rule text. Omit entirely for API/cloud-service-backed plugins (the common case).

readme_body.description: The README's main body text. If any source ever gathered for this plugin (this session or an earlier one, via sources.md) was flagged with a non-permissive license (license_ok: false), a 'License Notice' section listing just those sources is appended automatically; otherwise nothing sources-related is added here. The complete source history lives separately in sources.md, not README.md.

custom_param_docs.description: Rich, user-friendly markdown/html/text documentation for the customer-facing config fields declared in server_entry.customParams -- rendered verbatim into a self.poly.setCustomParamsDoc(...) call PG3 shows on the plugin's configuration page. Required whenever server_entry.customParams is non-empty (write real, helpful explanations -- e.g. where to find an API key, what format an IP address should be in -- never just the minimal values from customParams itself). Omit when server_entry.customParams is empty; a plugin with no customParams falls back to any POLYGLOT_CONFIG.md file in its own directory instead.

tests.description: Generated test files, as {filename: python_source} (filenames should start with 'test_').

iteration_note.description: A short note on what this generation call changed -- appended to context.md so a later session (or read_generated_plugin) can see the plugin's iteration history.

confirm_overwrite.description: Set true only after the customer has explicitly agreed to overwrite an existing plugin's files (the first call without this returns the conflict list and writes nothing).
